 Order

This miscellaneous appeal, under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, has been filed against the Award dated 21/07/2010 passed by III Additional Judge to the Court of I Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Gwalior in Claim Case No. 182/2009, by which the Insurance Company has been exonerated on the ground that offending vehicle was not having valid permit at the time of accident.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. It is submitted by counsel for the appellants that the Claims Tribunal has awarded less compensation amount.
3. Facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that on 20/5/2008 deceased Bhupat Lal lost his life in a vehicular accident.
It is the case that on 19/05/2008, deceased Bhupat Lal was going to Village Gader in Bus No. MP-06-B-1783.

On account of rash and negligent driving of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19544 2 MA-1858-2010 respondent no.1 Ramnaresh,
the Bus turned turtle.

As a result, Bhupat received grievous injuries and, ultimately, on 20/5/2008,
he expired.
4. It is the case of appellants that Bhupat was aged about 34 years and was a vegetable vendor.
He was earning Rs.4,500/- per month.
Challenging the Award passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is Laturi Singh Kushwah vs Ramnaresh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171313375/

1 submitted that Claims Tribunal has committed material illegality by taking monthly income of Bhupat as Rs.2,500/- and Claims Tribunal has also wrongly held that the Insurance Company would not be liable as the vehicle was being plied without any valid permit.
5 . Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by counsel for the respondents.
6. Heard, learned counsel for the parties.
7. Whether Insurance Company is liable in absence of valid permit ?

The Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Challa Upendra Rao reported in (2004) 8 SCC 517 has held as under :
"12.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Challa Upendra Rao reported in (2004) 8 SCC 517
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The High Court was of the view that since there was no permit, the question of violation of any condition thereof does not arise.
The view is clearly fallacious.
A person without permit to ply a vehicle cannot be placed on a better pedestal vis--vis one who has a permit, but has violated any condition thereof.
Plying of a vehicle without a permit is an infraction.
Therefore, in terms of Section 149(2) defence is available to the insurer on that aspect.
The acceptability of the stand is a matter of adjudication.
The question of policy being operative had no relevance for the issue regarding liability of the insurer.
The High Court was, therefore, not justified in holding the insurer liable."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19544 3 MA-1858-2010 The Supreme Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. reported in (2018)7 SCC 558 has held

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. reported in (2018)7 SCC 558
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that in case, if the transport vehicle was being plied without permit, then the Insurance Company would not be liable

Since the vehicle was being plied without permit, therefore, it is clear that the Vehicle was being plied contrary to the Insurance policy and, thus, the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by exonerating the Insurance Company.

However, the Claims Tribunal should have applied the principle of Pay and Recover and should have directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount with right to recover the same from the owner.

Therefore, the complete exoneration of Insurance Company is liable to be set aside and by applying the principle of Pay and Recover, it is directed that the Insurance Company shall pay the compensation amount with liberty to recover the same from owner of the offending vehicle in the same proceedings.
Income of deceased Bhupat :
The Claims Tribunal has held that appellants have failed to prove that Bhupat was a vegetable vendor and was earning Rs.4,500/- per month.
No arguments were advanced to challenge the said finding.
Therefore, it is clear that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by holding that appellants have failed to prove the monthly income of deceased Bhupat.

sentences.text: Now the next question for consideration is that in absence of any NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19544 4 MA-1858-2010 cogent evidence with regard to income of deceased, what should be the criteria for ascertaining notional monthly income of deceased ?
9. The Claims Tribunal has rightly held that appellant no.1 Laturi Singh/father of deceased is not entitled to claim compensation as he was not dependent upon the deceased.

So far as appellant no.2 Smt. Rambeti, appellant no.3 Ku. Sadhna and appellant no.4 Ku. Suninda are concerned, they are respectively mother and two minor daughters of the deceased and the Tribunal has also rightly held that they were dependent on the deceased, thus they are entitled for maintenance amount.
10. Although the claim petition was filed by parents and minor daughters of deceased Bhupat, but there is no pleading with regard to wife of Bhupat.
However, as Bhupat was looking after his two minor daughters, therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that monthly notional income assessed by Tribunal as Rs.2,500/- is on lower side.
Therefore, it is enhanced to Rs.3000/- per month.

Accordingly, appellant nos 2 to 4 are entitled for following maintenance amount:-
 S.No. Head Compensation  1. Monthly Income Rs.3,000/-
 2. Future prospects @ 40% Rs.1,200/-

3 . Total Monthly Income Rs.4,200/-
 4. Personal Expenses @ 1/3rd Rs.1,400/-
 5. Loss of yearly dependency Rs.33,600/-
 6. Multiplier @ 16 Rs.5,37,600/
 7. Loss of Estate @ 15000 Rs.15,000/-
 8. Loss of consortium 40,000 x 3 Rs.1,20,000/
 9.

Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 10.

Total compensation Rs.6,87,600/

Compensation paid by Tribunal Rs.3,50,660/
 12.

Compensation enhanced by Rs.3,36,940/

The remaining conditions of the Award shall remain the same.
